bodies.intuition: Diffusion learns to undo noise step by step. Flow matching asks a simpler question: what velocity field carries the simple distribution to the data one, in a straight line if possible? Train a network to predict that velocity, then integrate it. Straighter paths mean fewer integration steps, which is most of why newer image and video models sample so much faster.
bodies.engineer: The objective is a plain regression onto a target velocity, with no noise schedule to tune and no variational bound to derive — which is why it has largely displaced the diffusion formulation in new work even though the two are closely related. Path straightness is the design variable: an optimal-transport-shaped path needs far fewer function evaluations at sampling time than a curved one.
bodies.math: Regress v_θ(x_t, t) onto the conditional velocity of a chosen probability path. With the linear path x_t = (1−t)x_0 + t·x_1 the target is simply x_1 − x_0, constant along the path — so sampling is integrating an ODE rather than simulating an SDE, and a straight path is exactly integrable in one step.
